name: Roth
subtitle: thick sweet fried bread studded with poppy seeds, made for pann

ingredients.note: the moyan, rubbed into the flour
ghee is traditional if you can spare it

prepNotes: Dissolve the sugar in the warm milk first and let it cool to blood heat — undissolved sugar makes the dough grainy and the crust patchy.
Rub the warm ghee into the flour until the mixture holds its shape when squeezed in your fist; this moyan is what makes roth short and crumbly rather than chewy.
Rest the kneaded dough, covered, for 20 minutes before shaping.

steps.text: Rub the warm ghee thoroughly into the maida and salt with your fingertips for 4 minutes, until the flour looks like damp breadcrumbs.
steps.tip: Squeeze a handful — if it holds together in a lump, you have enough fat worked in.

steps.text: Add the crushed cardamom and fennel seeds, then pour in the sweetened milk a little at a time.
Bring it together into a stiff dough and knead just 2 minutes, no more.
steps.tip: Over-kneading develops gluten and gives you a tough, bready roth. Stop as soon as it is smooth.

steps.text: Divide into 6 balls, flatten each into a disc about 12cm across and 1cm thick, and press poppy seeds generously over both sides.
steps.tip: Press the seeds in firmly with the heel of your hand or they scatter into the oil.

steps.text: Prick each disc all over with a fork, right through.
steps.tip: The holes stop the roth ballooning and let it cook evenly to the middle.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai to about 160C — a scrap of dough should take a full 10 seconds to rise.
steps.tip: Lower and slower than you think. Hot oil browns the outside while the centre stays raw.

steps.text: Slide in one or two discs and fry for 4 to 5 minutes a side, turning once, until they are a deep even biscuit-brown and firm to the touch.
Lift onto a rack and let them cool completely; they crisp as they cool.
Repeat with the rest, letting the oil settle back to temperature between batches.

storage: Keeps 8 to 10 days in an airtight tin at room temperature and is meant to be eaten at that age. Do not refrigerate, which makes it damp.
